full_judgment:
2. The facts giving rise to this Second Appeal is that one Jaha Boksh had title in the land recorded in Khatian No.37 of Mouza Mohanagar. The plaintiff and his two brother's sons Tamjuddin and Taibur Rahman Goechu took settlement of 47 decimal land of Dag No.460 under Jahan Boksh and recorded in Khatian No.38. By amicable arrangement the plaintiff alone got the land. Thereafter, the plaintiff took the settlement of the remaining 2.12 decimals of this Khatian and 65 decimals of Khatian No. 39 from Jahan Boksh and the rent for the entire 3.24 acres was fixed at Rs. 13/-, Jaha Boksh thereafter granted the Amalanam dated 2" Poush, 1355 B.S. Since then the plaintiff is in possession. Subsequently on rth Jaistha, 1356 B.S. the plaintiff executed a Kabuliat in avour of Jaha Boksh. Part of Dag No. 472 was previously cultivable but in the C.S. record the entire Dag has been mentioned Beel (Mershy land/fishery). In 1355 B.S. and in 1356 B.S. the plaintiff excavated three tanks in parts of the suit land and thus raised the level of the part of the suit land. The plaintiff has also 9 fishing ditches. The plaintiff grows paddy on the part of the suit land. He also grew jute in the year 1367 B.S. The defendants along with others forcibly took away the jute grown by plaintiff on 2½ bights of land and the plaintiff had to file S.C.C. Suit No.49 of 1961 for compensation. But that suit was dismissed on the finding that jute was not grown. Since then the defendants were threatening to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land. Hence the plaintiff had to bright this suit for declaration of his title over the 2.12 acres of Dag No.475 and for confirmation of possession. At the time hearing, the plaintiff, however, made a prayer for recovery of possession alleging that the defendants had, in the meantime, dispossessed him when his prayer for temporary injunction was rejected. 

 3. Defendants Nos. 1, 3 and 4 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. Their case is that the suit land is a beel and is not cultivable and nothing is grown there. They are in possession since the time of their predecessors adverse to the title of Jaha Boksh as well as the plaintiff by catching fish from the ditches and using the weeds and water hyacinth as cattle fodder. They further stated that in C.S. Khatian Jahan Boksh got his name recorded fraudulently but being unable to possess the same, he inducted the defendants as tenants at a rent of Rs. 9/- and realized rent from them. The suit is barred by limitation the so called Amalnama granted by Jaha Baksh and Kabuliat of the plaintiff are forged.
